neighbours.label: ' lips' as a part that moves or shows feeling, as against lips mentioned as a static feature
fire: Her lips curled into a slow smile.
His lips tightened as he read the note.
She bit back a laugh, lips pressed together.
The boy's lips quivered and he looked away.
His lips parted in surprise at the news.
Her lips twisted at the thought of it.
He frowned, lips thinning into a line.
Her lips moved silently through the prayer.
quiet: She has very thin lips like her father.
He put balm on dry lips in the winter.
A cold sore appeared on her upper lips.
The doll has red lips and blue glass eyes.
With chapped lips and a cold, he stayed in.
The statue's lips are worn with age.
She applied some gloss to her lips at noon.
Bees stung the horse on its soft lips.

notes: Second round. In round 1 ' lips' read 0.43-1.02 when moving or showing feeling, but 0.03-0.06 in 'pale lips' and 'touched her lips'. Near misses here keep the word, so this tests the use.
